key_insight: AVS-HOBO makes constrained TSP optimization more practical on NISQ devices by reusing otherwise invalid states and removing one penalty term, improving VQE reliability without changing the problem goal.
engineering_relevance: The approach offers a more hardware-friendly encoding strategy for quantum optimization workflows, potentially reducing circuit/energy overhead for real device experiments.
method: Build a HOBO Hamiltonian with an efficient binary representation for TSP.
Introduce an all-valid-state HOBO (AVS-HOBO) using cyclic mapping to eliminate one penalty term.
Evaluate VQE performance in noiseless simulations and on real quantum hardware with error mitigation.
evidence_signal: The paper reports tests on TSP instances up to 20 cities, comparing original HOBO vs AVS-HOBO across convergence, approximation, tour-length, and feasibility metrics in simulation and on different quantum chips.
watch_item: Results depend on NISQ-era hardware noise, device architecture, and error-mitigation choices, so gains may vary across platforms and problem instances.
paper_title: All-valid-state HOBO encoding for constrained combinatorial optimization on NISQ devices
